chunks: And Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام:
"Indeed, the disbeliever visits his family and sees what displeases him, while what he loves is concealed from him."

key_terms.أَهْلَهُ: his family; his household or close people
key_terms.الْكَافِرَ: the disbeliever; the one described as experiencing deprivation after death
key_terms.يَزُورُ: visits; returns to observe or come upon
key_terms.يَكْرَهُهُ: what displeases him; what he finds hateful or distressing
key_terms.يُحِبُّ: he loves; what would please or comfort him
key_terms.يُسْتَرُ: is concealed; is hidden from view

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about a disbeliever visiting their family after death?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the disbeliever visits his family after death, but is shown only what causes distress, while what would please him is hidden. It points to a condition in the afterlife in which perception itself becomes part of punishment and deprivation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.543 - Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as):
"Indeed, the disbeliever visits their family and sees what displeases them, while what they would like is concealed from them (by the accompanying angels)."
